references.text: Moses gives instructions to the elders of Israel about slaughtering the Passover lamb, an elaboration on the Passover command.
The command to eat unleavened bread in haste as a reminder of the exodus from Egypt.
The explanation of the meaning of the Passover meal as the Lord's Passover, when He passed over the houses of the Israelites.
Elijah girded his cloak around his waist and ran ahead of Ahab, a parallel to having one's loins girded.
Righteousness shall be the belt around His loins, a messianic prophecy using the same imagery.
The prophet Jeremiah is told to gird up his loins and prepare for service.
Jesus exhorts the disciples to have their loins girded and lamps burning, ready for the Lord's coming.
Peter urges believers to gird up the loins of their minds and be ready, with a direct reference to Passover preparation.
Paul speaks of having truth as the belt around one's waist, part of God's full armor.
By faith Moses kept the Passover meal and sprinkled the blood so that the destroyer would not touch the firstborn.
Christ is our Passover lamb who has been sacrificed, a fulfillment of the meaning of Passover.
The staff as a shared symbol of God's authority and readiness during the exodus.
